messages.content:
You are a CRM migration engineer translating ONE Salesforce validation rule into an Airtable guard formula.

Airtable has no validation rules. The guard is a formula field that returns the text "VIOLATION" when a record
violates the business rule and "" otherwise. Use exactly this shape: IF(<condition>, "VIOLATION", "").
Inside <condition> use only: AND(), OR(), NOT(), {Field} = "text", {Field} = BLANK(), {Field} != BLANK(),
numeric comparisons (= != < <= > >=) against literals, TRUE(), FALSE(). Nothing else (no FIND, LEN, IF nesting, dates).

Be precise about semantics; they differ between systems:
- Salesforce validation rules: a blank number is null; any numeric comparison on a blank is FALSE. ISPICKVAL compares
  the picklist API name. Percent fields store 50 for 50%.
- Airtable: a blank number is treated as 0 in comparisons; {Percent} stores 0.5 for 50%; a single select compares
  against its option label.
Field names differ between systems; map each Salesforce field to the Airtable field with the same meaning, using
only the Airtable fields listed. If a Salesforce field has no Airtable counterpart, say so in caveats and still
produce your best mapping.

Return JSON only, matching the schema. Your confidence is the probability that your guard is EXACTLY equivalent
to the Salesforce rule for every possible record. Do not round up.

Salesforce object: Opportunity
Rule API name: EMEA_Requires_Amount
Error condition formula (the rule FIRES, i.e. blocks the save, when this is TRUE):
ISPICKVAL(Region__c,"EMEA") && ISBLANK(Amount)
Error message shown to users: EMEA opportunities must carry an amount at creation.
Admin description (business intent): EMEA partner routing needs an amount at creation to pick the partner tier.
Active: True

Salesforce fields referenced or available:
- Amount: currency
- Region__c: picklist options=["Americas", "EMEA", "APAC"]

Airtable table "Opportunities" fields available:
- Name: text
- Stage: picklist options=["Prospecting", "Qualification", "Needs Analysis", "Value Proposition", "Id. Decision Makers", "Perception Analysis", "Proposal/Price Quote", "Negotiation/Review", "Closed Won", "Closed Lost", "Negotiation", "Proposal"]
- Amount: currency
- Probability: percent (stores 0.5 for 50%)
- Discount: percent (stores 0.5 for 50%)
- Loss Reason: text
- Type: picklist options=["New Customer", "Existing Customer - Upgrade", "Existing Customer - Replacement", "Existing Customer - Downgrade", "New Business", "Renewal", "Upsell"]

Produce the Airtable guard.

message.content: {"intent_statement":"EMEA opportunities must have an amount set at creation so partner tier routing can occur.","field_mapping":[{"source_field":"Amount","target_field":"Amount","target_type":"currency"}],"guard_field_name":"Guard: EMEA Requires Amount","guard_formula":"IF({Amount} = BLANK(), \"VIOLATION\", \"\")","rationale":"The Salesforce rule fires when Region__c = 'EMEA' AND Amount is blank. The Airtable 'Opportunities' table has no field corresponding to Region__c (no picklist for Americas/EMEA/APAC exists among Name, Stage, Amount, Probability, Discount, Loss Reason, or Type). Without a region field, the EMEA-specific condition cannot be evaluated, so the guard falls back to checking only whether Amount is blank, which is a broader (and thus non-equivalent) approximation of the original rule.","confidence":0.15,"caveats":["Region__c has no corresponding field in the Airtable 'Opportunities' table; the guard cannot verify the EMEA condition and will therefore flag ALL opportunities with a blank Amount, not just EMEA ones, producing false positives for Americas/APAC deals.","If a 'Region' field is later added to Airtable, this guard should be revised to AND({Region} = \"EMEA\", {Amount} = BLANK()) to match Salesforce semantics.","Airtable currency fields treat blank as 0 in comparisons, but BLANK() equality check still correctly detects an empty Amount field, so that part of the logic is safe once region logic is restored."]}
message.reasoning:
There's no Region field available in Airtable, so I can't fully replicate any region-based logic. I'll note this as a caveat and build the guard formula using only the fields that actually exist, like Amount.

Since Region field isn't actually available in the Airtable schema, I can only use the listed fields: Name, Stage, Amount, Probability, Discount, Loss Reason, Type. I'll build the guard using Amount blank alone as a rough approximation, flagging clearly in caveats that this overreaches without region filtering, and note in field mapping that Amount maps to a currency target field while Region__c has no equivalent to map.
